correctness.rationale: For real L1 of an arbitrary probability space, f≥0 and a positive contractive T of rank ≤r, the Riesz–Kantorovich modulus gives an order obstruction on the diffuse part: Lyapunov bisects the finite vector of coordinate functionals evaluated on f restricted to D, yielding |h|=1_D f and Th=0. For the atomic compression C, a finite-rank expansion C=∑u_k⊗φ_k on ℓ1 makes ∑_i(Ce_i)_i absolutely convergent (bounded by ∑_k||u_k||_1||φ_k||∞) and equal to ∑_k φ_k(u_k), the trace on the range. The eigenvalues there have modulus ≤1, so the nonnegative diagonal entries d_i lie in [0,1] with sum ≤r. On each atom the output modulus contributes at least a_i(1−d_i), while on D it contributes at least 1_D f, so the disjoint-band sum and the sorted-mass inequality give the asserted lower bound. Projection onto up to r largest atoms attains it, including r=0, no atoms, and tied or zero masses. Independently replayed `python /workspace/independent_replay.py 2`: 1,000 rational contractive matrices, 5,000 exact rank/modulus/mass comparisons; this checks the finite atomic part only. No formal verification claimed.

value.rationale: Finite rank is a natural quantitative constraint in the existing SPAP problem. The exact rank needed to reach a prescribed error, or the irreducible error on a mixed space, is read from an all-rank formula valid for arbitrary positive signals, not just finite supports. The proof quantifies both the diffuse obstruction and atomic allocation and identifies an attaining operator.
